slot.brief: Rational function with a quadratic denominator; resolve into partial fractions (repeated linear factor) and integrate.

verdicts.working: Rewrite the integrand as $\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{2}{(x+1)^2}$. Integrating gives $\ln|x+1|-\frac{2}{x+1}+C$.

working:
$x^2+2x+1=(x+1)^2$\n$\dfrac{x+3}{(x+1)^2}=\dfrac{1}{x+1}+\dfrac{2}{(x+1)^2}$\n$\displaystyle\int=\ln|x+1|-\dfrac{2}{x+1}+C$

Independent check: Rewrite the integrand as $\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{2}{(x+1)^2}$. Integrating gives $\ln|x+1|-\frac{2}{x+1}+C$.
solution:
Factor the denominator and split the integrand:
$$\frac{x+3}{x^2+2x+1}=\frac{1}{x+1}+\frac{2}{(x+1)^2}.$$
Hence, $\displaystyle\int \frac{x+3}{x^2+2x+1}\,dx=\ln|x+1|-\frac{2}{x+1}+C$.
